items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve history when refreshing the PR base**

When `main` advances after GitHub creates the pull-request merge SHA but before this job runs, `git fetch --depth=1` marks the new `origin/${BASE_REF}` tip as a shallow boundary, undoing the preceding full-history checkout. The subsequent three-dot diff then fails with `fatal: ... no merge base`, so all three required public-bootstrap contexts fail instead of classifying the PR; the identical fetch in `private-bootstrap` has the same problem. This is reproducible in a full clone by advancing the base and fetching it with this command, and `git fetch -h` describes `--depth` as changing shallow history. Fetch without the depth limit, or diff against the event's fixed base SHA.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: moriya-fumio-thd
items.body: Disposition (orchestrator, final head d6343494): `fixed:e872f69f` — every fetch keeps full history (no `--depth=1` on the base refresh), so the three-dot diff always has a merge-base; reproduced (rc 128) and covered by the new test that moves origin/main after the head.
